A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeneMAN, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations and a 40-participant user study in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative comparisons across body proportions in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The human-specific diffusion priors, NeRF-to-DMTet geometry pipeline, texture refinement stages and losses remain unchanged. Section 4.2 explicitly lists video and synthetic training data already reflected in v2's dataset ablation; this does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The training-source inventory and counts remain unchanged, as do CAPE and in-the-wild evaluation coverage. Full-body, half-body and head-shot inputs were already evaluated in v2; v3's new table separates results within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark, geometry, qualitative and timing comparisons. The new body-proportion table reuses PIFu, while the existing PIFu/GTA/TeCH/SiTH comparison remains intact.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an evaluation organized into three body-proportion groups using the existing metrics. The established 50-sample, 120-view evaluation, CAPE comparison without ground-truth body poses and user-study design are retained. New per-group sample counts are unspecified.

E4.justification: v3 adds a quantitative robustness analysis across full-body, half-body and head-shot inputs in Appendix C.2/Table 3. v2 provided pooled scores and qualitative examples for this issue. Existing pipeline, prior-model and dataset ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based repetitions, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The user-study participant and comparison counts are unchanged, and the new table continues reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports GeneMAN/PIFu PSNR values of 32.529/28.039 for full-body, 28.245/25.383 for half-body and 26.374/25.047 for head-shot inputs, alongside LPIPS and CLIP similarity. Table 1 and v2 Tables 3–5, renumbered 4–6 in v3, retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The diffusion preliminaries, SDS formulations and reconstruction objectives in Equations 1–9 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about template-free reconstruction, human-specific priors and generalization across clothing, poses, belongings and body proportions. The new analysis supports an existing claim.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an explicit rationale for comparing only with PIFu: template-based approaches are described as unreliable for head-shot and half-body inputs. Existing interpretations of geometric ambiguity and limitations concerning runtime, hands, occlusion and complex objects are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 clarifies the 3D-prior training-data description by explicitly including videos and synthetic data. The geometric-metric description drops the earlier bidirectional/one-directional parentheticals. Detailed hyperparameters, hardware, timing and access links otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added: 2K-resolution human digitization, 3D Gaussian Splatting, DiFU, MVHumanNet and PKU-DyMVHumans. Research positioning receives limited refinements. The text-to-3D and general image-to-3D discussion moved into Section 2 already existed in v2's appendix.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained with localized edits. Supplementary related work moves into Section 2, references move before the appendix, and appendix sections are reorganized. Affiliations are updated, and acknowledgments and a broader-impacts section are added.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column NeurIPS formatting. Workflow Figures 2–4 are revised, figures and tables are resized and repositioned, Table 2 is restructured, and a new Table 3 is inserted. Existing qualitative reconstruction images are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the body-proportion claim by adding group-specific quantitative evidence where v2 relied on pooled metrics and qualitative examples, and clarifies the prior-training description. The gain is limited because the new comparison includes only PIFu and omits per-group sample counts and uncertainty. The core method and established results remain unchanged.
